evidence: The New Delta needs a 170 km canal with 13 pumping stations to move treated drainage water west (The National, May 2026).
root_causes: Fixed Nile allocation, upstream GERD uncertainty and population growth. Old-lands irrigation still relies on flood methods, and megaprojects depend on energy-intensive pumping of treated drainage water.
title: Water scarcity and Nile dependence

evidence: MoALR targets only 50% wheat self-sufficiency. Local maize covers about 55% of need, and the red-meat target is 60% (Egypt Today, April 2026).
root_causes: Limited arable land, low feed self-sufficiency and smallholder fragmentation.
title: Persistent wheat and red-meat import gaps

evidence: The New Delta is operated by Future of Egypt, with AFEA and NSPO as main implementers (The National, May 2026).
root_causes: Megaprojects are run by the Future of Egypt Authority and armed-forces bodies. Data is opaque, and blended or private finance for smallholders is limited.
title: State- and military-led delivery crowds out private and smallholder models

evidence: Donor-led AgriTech4Egypt (2026) aims to support only 105 startups over three years. Most agritech funding rounds are undisclosed or seed-stage.
root_causes: Fragmented holdings, an ageing public extension workforce and a small agri-tech VC pool.
title: Weak extension and smallholder tech adoption in the old lands

evidence: Pumping-based conveyance at the New Delta and Toshka. Wilo and Hassan Allam hold pump and irrigation contracts in Toshka.
root_causes: Desert agriculture depends on lifting water, and power shortages hit Egypt in 2024-25.
title: Energy cost of pumping and desalination-linked expansion

evidence: Agricultural dams at 26% fill in Jan 2025; 1.7bn m3/yr desalination target by 2030 (MWN, Jul 2025)
root_causes: Climate change, groundwater over-extraction, export-crop water intensity
title: Structural water scarcity and drought

evidence: Generation Green mid-term review commissioned (BCG, 11.8m MAD) to recalibrate (Africa24, Jul 2026)
root_causes: Investment skewed to irrigated export farms; small farm size; low insurance uptake
title: Dualistic sector: rain-fed smallholders lag

evidence: Ongoing melkisation of collective lands under Generation Green
root_causes: Collective (soulaliyate), habous and undivided family lands limit titling and credit
title: Land tenure complexity

evidence: Renaming of ministry to include 'Food Sovereignty' in Oct 2026 signals domestic supply priority
root_causes: Drought-reduced pasture and feed costs; import dependence for feed grains
title: Livestock herd and feed shock

evidence: Government linking renewables to agriculture to secure food and water (Hespress)
root_causes: Desalination is energy-intensive; renewables integration still scaling
title: Energy cost of desalinated irrigation water

evidence: AFOR: about 1.75 million ha certified at 30 Sept 2026 (~2 million ha by Oct) and 67% of villages delimited (Fraternité Matin, 7 Oct 2026).
root_causes: Customary tenure, slow and costly certification under the 1998 Rural Land Law, and conflicts between migrants and autochthonous communities.
title: Rural land tenure insecurity

evidence: PNIA 3 lists food sovereignty as axis 1. Food crops grew 9% in 2025 but remain largely rain-fed.
root_causes: Investment has historically favoured export crops. Irrigation schemes and mechanization for lowland rice are limited.
title: Food-crop productivity, rice imports and low irrigation

evidence: PNIA 3 adds a dedicated axis on 'mécanismes de financement renforcés'. The PM calls for 'une agriculture d'entreprise, mieux financée' (June 2026).
root_causes: Banks see high risk, untitled land cannot serve as collateral, and agricultural insurance is weak.
title: Thin agricultural credit and finance

evidence: FIRCA has published a cocoa and coffee orchard-regeneration guide. The CCC focuses on youth succession (JNCC, Sept 2026).
root_causes: Swollen-shoot virus, ageing trees and farmers, and EUDR traceability requirements.
title: Ageing cocoa orchards, disease and deforestation compliance

evidence: The agropoles programme has been in rollout since 2019 and is still being implemented.
root_causes: Slow PPP structuring and delays in feeder infrastructure.
title: Incomplete agro-industrial zones (agropoles)

evidence: Only about 210,000 ha developed vs 1.9 million ha potential (Graphic, 2018). MiDA in March 2026 found the Subinja scheme stripped of pumps and transformer, and a rice scheme using 300 of 1,000 acres.
root_causes: Chronic under-funding, incomplete dams, vandalism and weak scheme management. A long-planned shift to private O&M was never fully realized.
title: Very low irrigated area and poor O&M of existing schemes

evidence: MoFA vs MoF dispute (June 2026): H1 allotment capped at GH¢910m, Feed Ghana line GH¢4.5m, against MoF's claim of GH¢1.6bn released.
root_causes: IMF-era fiscal consolidation, cash-based allotments, and each new government replacing its predecessor's flagship programme.
title: Budget releases and policy discontinuity

evidence: COCOBOD CEO cites GH¢26bn in road contracts and other legacy debts. Stranded beans in 2026. Pivot to processors announced Feb 2026.
root_causes: COCOBOD's syndicated-loan model broke down, leaving legacy debt, pricing mismatches and dependence on raw-bean exports.
title: Cocoa sector debt and low local processing

evidence: The rice-seed independence target (10,000 t by 2027) is still under development via the Korea Rural Cooperation project.
root_causes: Fragmented smallholdings, little tractor-hire finance and dependence on imported seed.
title: Low mechanization and seed self-sufficiency

evidence: NAFCO buffer stock allocated only GH¢30m in the H1 2026 allotment.
root_causes: Limited warehousing and buffer-stock financing, and poor feeder roads.
title: Post-harvest losses and weak storage and market links

evidence: 842 deaths and 279 abductions in 156 incidents in May 2026 (Nextier, via AllAfrica Jul 2026)
root_causes: Banditry, kidnapping and farmer-herder conflict; weak rural policing; land-use competition
title: Insecurity displacing farmers in core food belts

evidence: 2026 allocation N1.45trn (~2.4-2.8%) vs 10% target; in 2019 only N44.96bn released of N137.9bn approved
root_causes: Oil-revenue volatility; recurrent-heavy spending; poor release discipline; limited transparency
title: Low and poorly executed public agriculture spending

evidence: About 154,000 ha irrigated (AllAfrica Jul 2026); NISER flags irrigation scale-up as under-funded
root_causes: Under-maintained river-basin authority dams; energy cost of pumping; rain-fed reliance
title: Minimal irrigation

evidence: AfDB rated SAPZ unsatisfactory with 12% disbursement (AllAfrica Jul 2026)
root_causes: Complex multi-tier (federal, state, private) governance; counterpart funding delays; off-site power and roads not ready
title: Agro-processing zones slow to deliver

evidence: Storage and cold chain capacity reported far below need; NISER cites under-funded mechanisation and extension
root_causes: Unreliable grid supply, diesel dependence, fragmented aggregation
title: Storage, cold chain and power deficit

evidence: Public budget still finances ~78% of ag spending but inputs remain import-dependent (FAO MAFAP); recurrent fertiliser shortages reported
root_causes: Chronic forex shortages; state-controlled fertiliser procurement; delayed deliveries
title: FX scarcity and input import dependence

evidence: 2024 Proclamation 1324 allows leasing and collateralising use-rights; only ~2.2bn birr in certificate-backed credit by Jan 2024
root_causes: Constitutional state ownership of land; small fragmented plots; use-rights only
title: Land tenure limits investment and finance

evidence: Disruption of input distribution and market access in key surplus zones
root_causes: Armed conflict in Amhara and parts of Oromia; legacy of Tigray war
title: Conflict and insecurity in core producing regions

evidence: Digital Agriculture Roadmap lists improving digital infrastructure and farmer digital literacy among its 32 priorities
root_causes: Late telecom liberalisation; low rural grid connections despite generation surplus
title: Weak rural digital and power distribution

evidence: Separate Ministry of Logistics created in the 2026 cabinet reflects the bottleneck
root_causes: Single dominant port corridor (Djibouti); weak feeder roads; limited cold chain
title: Landlocked, high-cost logistics

evidence: Ministry allocation of about Ksh75.49bn (~2.7% of budget); CS Kagwe told Parliament the sector is stuck near 3% against the 10% pledge (Citizen Digital, Feb 2026)
root_causes: Treasury ceilings do not match sector priorities; heavy debt service crowds out development spending; functions split between national government and counties
title: Chronic under-funding of agriculture

evidence: 664,000 irrigated acres in 2021/22 vs a 1.29m-acre target for 2027/28 under NISIP (Citizen Digital, Jun 2026)
root_causes: Rain-fed tradition; large-scheme failures (e.g. delays at Galana Kulalu); high capex and weak water-storage infrastructure
title: Low irrigation coverage in a mostly arid country

evidence: CS Kagwe warning on staff retirements; Feb 2026 budget testimony cites weak extension services
root_causes: Devolved extension under-funded by counties; hiring freezes; about half of ministry staff near retirement
title: Thin, ageing public extension system

evidence: Government rolled out 12.5m subsidised bags for the 2026 long rains via KIAMIS-registered farmers; high input costs cited by CS in Feb 2026
root_causes: Currency volatility; reliance on imported fertiliser; past fake-fertiliser scandals; delays in subsidy releases
title: Input costs and leakage in subsidy delivery

evidence: Jan 2026 30-day ultimatum to maize hoarders as government sought 4m bags for strategic reserves
root_causes: Fragmented smallholder aggregation; hoarding and price speculation; under-used warehouse receipt system
title: Post-harvest losses and weak storage for grains

evidence: ~75,223 ha irrigated (15% of 493,050 ha irrigable); target 132,961 ha by 2029 (MINAGRI via New Times, Feb 2026)
root_causes: Steep topography raises cost per hectare; marshland development is capital-intensive; dependence on donor financing
title: Low irrigation coverage on hilly terrain

evidence: Agriculture ~6% of commercial lending; NST2 target ≥10% (MINAGRI, Jul 2026)
root_causes: Perceived risk, small ticket sizes, limited collateral value of tiny plots
title: Thin commercial finance for agriculture

evidence: PSTA5 names land scarcity, low productivity and post-harvest losses among core challenges
root_causes: High population density, inheritance-driven subdivision; slopes limit mechanisation
title: Land scarcity and fragmentation

evidence: Government launched direct air-cargo for fresh produce to bypass ground constraints
root_causes: Distance to Mombasa and Dar es Salaam ports; reliance on road freight; limited cold chain
title: High-cost, landlocked logistics

evidence: 2026/27 MINAGRI budget increase mainly for fertiliser subsidies, post-harvest storage and strategic reserves (KT Press, Jul 2026)
root_causes: Full import dependence for fertiliser; global price shocks
title: Fertiliser price exposure

evidence: Agenda 10/30 targets 8.5 million ha irrigated. The borehole programme's first phase covers only ~13,500 acres, with 415 of 67,000 boreholes drilled (Aug 2026).
root_causes: Historically low capital budgets, slow scheme construction, and dependence on rain-fed smallholdings.
title: Irrigated area far below potential

evidence: Agenda 10/30 aims to cut post-harvest losses from 35% to 5% and lift processing from 10% to 50%. The avocado plan needs 20 new collection centres.
root_causes: Few aggregation centres, poor rural roads and unreliable rural power.
title: Post-harvest losses and weak cold chain and processing

evidence: NAESA is only beginning operations in July 2026. Crackdown on the fake-seed trade (Apr 2026).
root_causes: Understaffed extension service and limited TARI funding. Fake-seed trade undermines adoption.
title: Thin extension and research-to-farm delivery

evidence: Agenda 10/30 financing needs are estimated at TZS 33 trillion to 2030 (The Citizen). Agritech rounds are mostly pre-seed (MazaoHub $2m).
root_causes: High lending rates, land-tenure constraints on village land, and small TADB capitalization.
title: Limited private and agri finance and insurance

evidence: The BBT youth programme (TZS 1.1tn budget anchor) and NIRC equipment handovers are still early-stage.
root_causes: Hand-hoe dominance, the high cost of equipment, and an ageing farmer base.
title: Low mechanization and youth engagement

evidence: Largest FMD outbreak on record. 13.5 million vaccines imported to end-June 2026, and exports to China are conditional on biosecurity (Food For Mzansi, Sept 2026).
root_causes: Eroded state veterinary capacity, vaccine-supply shortfalls (Onderstepoort Biological Products) and litigation over FMD management.
title: Animal disease control and biosecurity

evidence: The minister cites neglected rural roads, an inefficient harbour and rail problems, and is engaging the transport and public works ministries (Sept 2026).
root_causes: Transnet's operational decline, under-maintained provincial roads and slow private participation in freight rail and ports.
title: Port, rail and rural-road bottlenecks

evidence: AAMP review (Jul 2026): limited access to blended finance for smallholders. Land Bank CEO resigned in Feb 2026 and an acting CEO was appointed.
root_causes: Land Bank instability, provincial red tape and weak risk-sharing instruments.
title: Limited finance and support for emerging/black farmers

evidence: AAMP stakeholders cite uneven provincial alignment and red tape. Expropriation Act implementation is contested.
root_causes: Slow redistribution and title transfer. Many beneficiaries lack title deeds, which limits their access to collateral.
title: Land reform and tenure uncertainty

evidence: Load-shedding years (2022-24) hit irrigation and cold chain, and agri-business sentiment remains sensitive to power and input costs.
root_causes: Eskom's generation deficit and tariff hikes raise the cost of pumping and cold storage.
title: Energy reliability and cost for irrigation and cold chain

evidence: ~6% of Africa's cropland is irrigated (~4% in SSA) vs ~37% in Asia; SSA withdraws only ~1% of its renewable water resources vs 219% in North Africa.
opportunity: Pay-as-you-go solar pumps bundled with input credit and offtake; farmer-led irrigation finance facilities; irrigation-as-a-service; policymakers can de-risk via results-based subsidies and groundwater mapping.
root_causes: High capital cost per irrigated ha, weak water governance and O&M of large public schemes, limited energy for pumping, little finance for small-scale/solar pumps, transboundary water politics.
title: Irrigation deficit: rain-fed farming dominates
who_is_working: AUDA-NEPAD/Africa Water Facility, World Bank (SIIP Sahel Irrigation Initiative), IWMI, FAO, AfDB TAAT; private: SunCulture, Futurepump, Oolu.

evidence: Africa used 22.6 kg/ha in 2023 (16.3 in 2000) vs a global average of 116.4 kg/ha and Asia 186 kg/ha; the 2006 Abuja target of 50 kg/ha remains unmet. The AU Action Plan baseline is 18 kg/ha (2020) and the target is 54 kg/ha by 2034. Paradoxically, Africa produces ~30 Mt of fertilizer a year, about 2x what it consumes.
evidence_source: FAO data via Africa Sustainability Matters (May 2026) https://africasustainabilitymatters.com/africa-still-far-below-fertilizer-targets-as-soil-degradation-threatens-food-security-and-agricultural-growth/ ; AU Africa Fertilizer & Soil Health Action Plan https://au.int/sites/default/files/documents/43208-doc-EN_Africa_Fertilizer_and_Soil_Health_Action_Plan.pdf
opportunity: Blending hubs near demand, digital soil maps/soil testing with crop-specific blends, agro-dealer networks with embedded credit, regional trade so African producers (Morocco, Nigeria) supply African farmers.
root_causes: Landed fertilizer prices 2-3x world prices due to port/inland logistics, small fragmented markets, FX shortages, weak soil testing and blanket recommendations, poorly targeted subsidy programs.
title: Very low fertilizer use and degrading soils
who_is_working: AU/AUDA-NEPAD (Fertilizer & Soil Health Action Plan), AfDB Africa Fertilizer Financing Mechanism, AFAP, IFDC, OCP Africa, Dangote/Indorama, AGRA, One Acre Fund.

evidence: Fewer than 2 tractors per 1,000 ha of cropland in Africa vs about 10 in South Asia and Latin America (FAO); ~70% of African farmers cultivate plots under 2 ha by hoe.
opportunity: Uber-for-tractors/custom hiring with IoT tracking and asset finance; two-wheel tractors and small machines suited to plots under 2 ha (the Bangladesh model); operator training academies.
root_causes: Small fragmented plots, no machinery finance or leasing, scarce spare parts and operators, import duties, collapse of 1970s state tractor schemes.
title: Mechanization: hoe-based smallholder agriculture
who_is_working: FAO/AU Sustainable Agricultural Mechanization Framework for Africa (SAMA), Hello Tractor, TROTRO Tractor, AGCO/John Deere dealer programs, AfDB TAAT, CIMMYT two-wheel tractor work.

evidence: SSA grain post-harvest losses are ~US$4bn/yr, ~15% of a ~US$27bn grain output (FAO/NRI 'Missing Food'); APHLIS cites Nigeria losing ~40% of food output, up to 70% for fruit and vegetables. The Kampala CAADP Declaration targets a 50% cut in post-harvest loss by 2035.
evidence_source: FAO/World Bank/NRI via Farming Online https://farming.co.uk/news/grain-losses-in-sub-saharan-africa-could-total-%244-billion ; The Star (Kampala targets) https://www.the-star.co.ke/business/2025-01-15-africa-to-increase-agrifood-output-by-45-in-a-decade
opportunity: Hermetic storage, mobile dryers and aggregation hubs; warehouse receipt finance; aflatoxin testing as a service.
root_causes: Poor on-farm storage, aflatoxin/pests, lack of drying equipment, bad roads delaying transport, no warehouse receipt systems, distress selling at harvest.
title: Post-harvest losses
who_is_working: APHLIS, Rockefeller Foundation YieldWise, WFP, AGRA, PICS bags (Purdue), Eastern Africa Grain Council, warehouse receipt systems (Kenya, Ethiopia ECX, Ghana GCX).

evidence: Cold storage is about 4.5 m3 per 1,000 people in Uganda (2023) and about 5 in Ethiopia vs ~38 in Kenya (GCCA 2020). India has 131 million m3 of refrigerated warehouse space. Nigeria reportedly meets less than 4% of its cold chain needs, a gap costing up to US$4.5bn/yr.
evidence_source: Refindustry / IJR study https://refindustry.com/news/market-research/uganda-s-cold-storage-capacity-assessed-at-4-5-m-per-1-000-inhabitants ; Cooling Post (GCCA) https://www.coolingpost.com/world-news/coldstore-capacity-in-india-greater-than-usa/ ; African Marketing Confederation https://africanmarketingconfederation.org/poor-cold-chain-logistics-resulting-in-massive-food-wastage-in-africa/
opportunity: Solar cold-rooms on pay-per-crate models, cooling-as-a-service, reefer logistics on export corridors, and pairing mini-grids with cold storage as an anchor load.
root_causes: Unreliable and expensive grid power, high capex, fragmented informal markets, few reefer trucks, weak food safety enforcement.
title: Cold chain almost absent for perishables
who_is_working: ColdHubs (Nigeria), Ecotutu, InspiraFarms, Koolboks, SokoFresh, Twiga-type aggregators, Africa Centre of Excellence for Sustainable Cooling (Rwanda), UNEP Cool Coalition.

evidence: Under 3% of commercial bank lending in Africa goes to agriculture (Buhari at Dakar 2, Jan 2023), even though agriculture is ~16% of GDP and ~60% of employment. Kenya's agriculture CS made the same ~3% point in 2025.
opportunity: Credit scoring from satellite, mobile money and input-purchase data; embedded finance in input and offtake contracts; credit guarantees and first-loss funds; national farmer registries (the AgriStack model) to cut KYC costs.
root_causes: Perceived high risk (weather, prices), no collateral because land is undocumented, high cost to serve dispersed farmers, sovereign yields crowding out private lending, lack of credit data.
title: Agri-finance starvation
who_is_working: AfDB, AGRA, Mastercard Foundation, NIRSAL (Nigeria), Kenya AFC, IFAD, Apollo Agriculture, Pula, FarmDrive, Aceli Africa, Root Capital.

evidence: Extension agent-to-farmer ratios in Africa commonly run 1:2,000 to 1:10,000 vs the FAO-recommended 1:500. The Fertilizer Action Plan aims for 70% of farmers to get effective agronomic advice by 2034.
evidence_source: AGRA CESSA https://cessa.agra.org/farmer-awareness-and-participation/ ; AU Fertilizer Action Plan https://au.int/sites/default/files/documents/43208-doc-EN_Africa_Fertilizer_and_Soil_Health_Action_Plan.pdf
opportunity: Local-language AI advisory over voice/WhatsApp/IVR, paid village-based advisors and agro-dealer agents, and public extension refocused on content quality and verification.
root_causes: Public hiring freezes since structural adjustment, low operating budgets (no fuel or transport), aging workforce, weak research-extension link, top-down messaging.
title: Extension systems spread too thin
who_is_working: Digital Green (Farmer.Chat), Ethiopia ATI 8028 hotline, One Acre Fund, Precision Development (PxD), CABI Plantwise, AFAAS, iShamba, Viamo/3-2-1.

evidence: Kenya (SSPI/TASAI 2023): certified seed meets 53% of maize demand but only 4% of beans; KALRO has just 48 breeders across 4 crops. Only 7 of 21 COMESA states had domesticated harmonized seed regulations by 2018.
opportunity: Seed authentication (scratch codes, QR), early-generation seed companies for legumes, quality-declared seed schemes, and regional catalogue listings to sell across 20+ markets with one release.
root_causes: Informal farmer-saved seed dominates, slow variety release, small breeder pools, counterfeit seed, fragmented national regulations, little private investment in self-pollinated crops (legumes, sorghum).
title: Weak formal seed systems
who_is_working: TASAI, AGRA, CIMMYT, CGIAR Seed Equal, AATF, Seeds2B (Syngenta Foundation), AFSTA, regional seed bodies (COMESA, SADC SSSN, ECOWAS/CORAF).

evidence: Only ~10% of Africa's rural land is registered. Land transfers take twice as long and cost twice as much as in industrialized countries. Ghana, Kenya and Uganda each have under 10 surveyors per million people (Malaysia: 197). Scaling reforms would cost ~US$4.5bn over 10 years.
opportunity: Low-cost drone/satellite plus community-validated mapping (fit-for-purpose land administration); digital certificates linked to farmer IDs so land rights can unlock credit.
root_causes: Dual customary/statutory systems, costly and slow registration, few surveyors, gender-biased inheritance, elite capture risk.
title: Insecure, undocumented land tenure
who_is_working: World Bank land administration projects, AU Land Policy Centre, Rwanda's land tenure regularization, Ethiopia's second-level certification, Medici Land Governance, Cadasta, Landesa.

evidence: Intra-African trade was US$220.3bn in 2024, roughly 15% of Africa's trade (Afreximbank). Africa ran a US$16.7bn agricultural trade deficit in 2023 (imports ~US$110bn, exports ~US$93.3bn), and only 5 countries are net agri exporters (AATM 2025). AfCFTA: 50 ratifications, but only 26 states had gazetted tariff schedules by June 2026.
opportunity: Cross-border B2B agri marketplaces, trade finance on PAPSS rails, SPS-compliant aggregation/testing, and regional brands that replace imported staples (rice, wheat, edible oil).
root_causes: Non-tariff barriers, SPS/standards differences, border delays, poor corridors, ad hoc export bans, payment/FX frictions, slow AfCFTA tariff gazetting.
title: Fragmented intra-African trade and an agri trade deficit
who_is_working: AfCFTA Secretariat, Afreximbank (PAPSS, AfCFTA Adjustment Fund), TradeMark Africa, regional economic communities, AKADEMIYA2063 (AATM).

evidence: West Africa grows over 70% of the world's cocoa but does only ~20% of global grinding, and ~75% of beans are exported raw. Only ~5% of Africa's cashew is processed before export; ~95% of raw nuts go to India/Vietnam. The Kampala target is to raise locally processed food to 35% of agrifood GDP by 2035.
opportunity: Mid-scale processing near farm clusters (cashew, cassava starch, soybean, tomato paste), tolling models, captive solar for agro-industrial parks, and export-processing incentives tied to AfCFTA rules of origin.
root_causes: Expensive, unreliable power, tariff escalation in importing markets, weak industrial finance, small/inconsistent raw-material supply, skills gaps, and export taxes/levies that favor raw exports.
title: Low processing and value addition
who_is_working: AfDB Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones (SAPZ), Afreximbank, Côte d'Ivoire/Ghana cocoa processing policies, African Cashew Alliance, Arise IIP (GDIZ Benin), UNIDO.

evidence: 563 million people in SSA lacked electricity in 2024, 86% of the global deficit (up from 49% in 2010). Rural people without power rose from 376m to 447m (2010-2024). Mission 300 reported 64m people connected (WBG 59m + AfDB 5m) by Oct 2026 toward 300m by 2030.
opportunity: Productive-use appliances (milling, cooling, pumping) as mini-grid anchor loads; agri-PUE financing; solar-powered processing hubs.
root_causes: Utilities financially distressed, low rural load density, high grid extension cost, tariff and subsidy distortions, currency risk for off-grid investors.
title: Rural electricity access gap
who_is_working: World Bank/AfDB Mission 300, SEforALL, Rockefeller/GEAPP, Power Africa (scaled back), mini-grid developers (Husk, CrossBoundary, Nuru), d.light, Sun King.

evidence: Most African countries have a Rural Access Index (share of rural people within 2 km of an all-season road) of 20-40%, vs a 68% world country average. Nigeria alone has ~75 million rural people without access. Globally ~1.17bn rural people lack access.
evidence_source: 'Rural Access Index: A global study' (arXiv 2023) https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.00505
opportunity: Performance-based feeder road maintenance contracts, trail bridges, geospatial road condition monitoring, and logistics platforms that aggregate loads to cut cost per km.
root_causes: Low maintenance budgets, reliance on unpaved earth roads cut off in rainy seasons, weak rural road agencies, focus on trunk corridors over feeder roads.
title: Poor rural road access
who_is_working: World Bank (SDG 9.1.1 custodian; rural roads projects), AfDB, SSATP, national roads funds, PIDA corridors, Bridges to Prosperity.

evidence: In SSA only 27% of the population (46% of adults) uses mobile internet. 60% live under coverage but don't use it (usage gap); 13% have no coverage (GSMA 2024).
opportunity: Voice/USSD-first and offline-capable agri apps, smartphone financing bundled with farm credit, and village digital agents.
root_causes: Smartphone affordability, data prices, digital literacy, lack of local-language content, gender gap, rural power for charging.
title: Digital connectivity: usage gap more than coverage gap
who_is_working: GSMA AgriTech, Safaricom DigiFarm, MTN, Airtel, Smart Africa, World Bank Digital Economy for Africa (DE4A), handset financing (M-KOPA).

evidence: The 50x2030 Initiative exists to close the agricultural data gap in 50 low- and middle-income countries by 2030 (largely in Africa). The 4th CAADP Biennial Review (2023) found no country on track, set against a 9.29 benchmark, partly because of data gaps. By contrast India created 110 million digital farmer IDs by Oct 2026.
evidence_source: Data4SDGs / 50x2030 https://www.data4sdgs.org/50by2030 ; ESAFF CAADP BR brief https://esaff.org/index-php/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Policy-Brief-SADC-Performance-in-the-CAADP-BR-Report-wb.pdf ; Swarajya https://swarajyamag.com/news-brief/digital-agriculture-mission-crosses-11-crore-farmer-ids-five-months-before-march-2027-deadline
opportunity: Interoperable farmer and land registries (open DPI), EO-based crop monitoring, and data cooperatives that let farmers monetize data under the AU Data Policy Framework.
root_causes: Underfunded national statistics offices, irregular agricultural censuses, no farmer registries, data siloed across ministries and donors, weak data-sharing rules.
title: Agricultural data and statistics gap
who_is_working: FAO/World Bank/IFAD 50x2030, AKADEMIYA2063/ReSAKSS, Digital Earth Africa, Lacuna Fund, GODAN, national farmer registries (Kenya KIAMIS, Rwanda Smart Nkunganire, Ethiopia).

evidence: Climate change has cut Africa's agricultural productivity growth by ~34% since 1961 (IPCC AR6/Ortiz-Bobea). Only ~6% of arable land is irrigated, so most farms are fully weather-exposed. Only ~3% of global climate finance reaches Africa. By comparison, the EU CAP supports risk-management tools for ~15% of EU farmers.
opportunity: Area-yield and satellite-index insurance bundled with credit and inputs, government-subsidized meso-level cover via cooperatives, and climate-smart seed plus advisory bundles.
root_causes: Rain-fed dependence, basis risk in index insurance, low awareness, premiums unaffordable without subsidy, weak weather-station networks, little adaptation finance.
title: Climate risk with little insurance cover
who_is_working: African Risk Capacity (ARC), AfDB ADRiFi, Pula, ACRE Africa, Kenya KLIP, Global Shield, CGIAR climate programs, TAHMO weather stations.

evidence: Only a handful of SSA countries reached the 1% of AgGDP research intensity target in 2016/17; ~60% of 49 countries with data were below 0.5%. SSA investment was 42% below attainable levels. Compare Brazil's Embrapa budget of R$3.4bn in 2017.
opportunity: Regional research consortia on shared crops; public-private breeding (gene editing under Kenya/Nigeria/Ghana guidelines); ag-research levies on exports (Brazil/Embrapa-style dedicated funding).
root_causes: Low government budgets, donor-dependent and volatile funding, aging scientists, small national systems that cannot reach scale.
title: Chronic underinvestment in agricultural R&D
who_is_working: CGIAR, FARA, ASARECA/CORAF/CCARDESA, AATF, national research institutes (EIAR, KALRO, CSIR), Gates Foundation, AU genome-editing database.

evidence: 10-12 million young Africans enter the workforce each year but only ~3 million formal jobs are created; the youth population will double to over 830 million by 2050 (AfDB Jobs for Youth strategy).
evidence_source: tralac / AfDB Jobs for Youth in Africa 2016-2025 https://tralac.org/news/article/9843-afdb-group-strategy-for-jobs-for-youth-in-africa-2016-2025.html
opportunity: Youth service-provider models (spraying, mechanization, aggregation, digital agents), agrifood SME accelerators, and apprenticeship-linked processing parks.
root_causes: Low farm profitability, lack of land and finance for young people, perception of farming as poverty, skills mismatch, slow off-farm agrifood growth.
title: Youth bulge without agrifood jobs
who_is_working: AfDB ENABLE Youth, Mastercard Foundation Young Africa Works, IITA Youth Agripreneurs, IFAD, AGRA, Kampala CAADP (women and youth commitment).
